note: Every study here was pre-registered: the question, data, costs, windows and pass rule were written and sealed (SHA-256 recorded beside the file, with the time) before the result was computed. A sidecar with several lines is a pre-registration that was re-sealed when an addendum was appended; the last line is the file as it stands. Figures are percent, ratio and count only. scripts/verify_evidence.py recomputes each seal from the committed file.

studies.title: Five slow daily rules on Bitget USDT-M perps, 2021-06 → 2026-10
studies.question: Is there a rule, on the data the bot already trades, that makes money after costs out of sample? Slower rules on longer history, every parameter fixed before the first run.
studies.data: Bitget USDT-M perpetual daily bars, 20 coins chosen ex ante (January 2022 market cap), 150 days of history before a coin is eligible; 0.10% per side; longs charged 0.03%/day funding.
studies.pass_rule: development Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND holdout Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND positive in ≥ 4 of 6 calendar years AND 90% block-bootstrap interval of the full-period Sharpe above 0 AND holdout drawdown no worse than BTC buy-and-hold's.
studies.verdict: none of the five passes; H1a trend long/short came nearest at development 0.66 / holdout 0.24
studies.limits: Survivorship (the 20 were chosen by 2022 market cap; LUNA and MATIC absent, stated not corrected); a 3-to-5-year Sharpe has a standard error near 0.8, so the study had little power; funding was a fixed assumption, revisited in funding_recost.

studies.title: Three funding-rate rules on Bitget USDT-M perps, 2023-10 → 2026-10
studies.question: Does the funding rate itself carry a tradable signal: a cross-sectional carry, a crowded-funding contrarian, or a crowded-funding filter on the trend rule?
studies.data: Bitget USDT-M perpetual daily prices with Hyperliquid funding as the proxy (Bitget's public funding history starts around July 2026); the primary universe, fixed from coverage alone, is the 9 coins with funding on every day from 2023-06-01: BTC ETH BNB SOL DOGE AVAX LTC ATOM LINK; 0.10% per side.
studies.pass_rule: development Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND holdout Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND 90% bootstrap interval above 0 AND holdout drawdown no worse than BTC's.
studies.verdict: none passes. Carry's funding leg is real (+4–10%/yr received every year), but weekly rebalancing costs about 5.3%/yr and the unhedged price leg decides the result; crowded funding kept going rather than reversing; the funding filter removed the trend rule's best days
studies.limits: A proxy venue's funding; the holdout's prices had been read by the Bitget study; low power (Sharpe s.e. ≈ 0.8).

studies.title: The same five rules on Kraken's spot history, 2014 → 2026
studies.question: Do the five rules hold on the earlier, unread history? The Bitget study's weakness was power.
studies.data: Kraken OHLCVT archive (sha256 bc273e90…e7b1c7), daily USD bars: the 16 of the earlier study's 20 coins with a Kraken USD pair and at least 150 daily bars before 2021-06-01 (AVAX, BNB, NEAR, SOL out); 0.10% per side; spot, so no funding.

windows.development: first day with two eligible coins (2014) → 2021-05-31
windows.holdout: 2021-06-01 → 2026-06-30 (prices read before on Bitget: a replication on another venue's prints, not a clean holdout)

studies.pass_rule: development Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND holdout Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND positive in ≥ 6 of the calendar years traded AND 90% bootstrap interval above 0 AND holdout drawdown no worse than BTC buy-and-hold's.
studies.verdict: H1b trend long-only passes every criterion (development 2.12, holdout 0.63, up in 8 of 13 years, bootstrap [1.05, 2.15], drawdown 10.1% against BTC's 76.7%); the other four fail on the holdout Sharpe
studies.limits: Survivorship as above; spot without funding flatters nothing on the long-only rule but flatters the long/short ones in 2013–2017; the holdout years were read before.

studies.title: The long-only trend sleeve re-costed with real perpetual funding, 2021-01 → 2026-06
studies.question: The Bitget study charged a fixed 0.03%/day of funding and read about zero; Kraken spot charged none and read the pass. What does a trend-following long book actually pay, and does the rule survive it?
studies.data: Kraken spot daily prices (the kraken_spot_history set) with Binance USDT-perp funding per 8-hour window from CoinAPI, 16 coins; a window with no sample is counted, never read as zero; 0.10% per side.

windows.window: 2021-01-01 → 2026-06-30 (the overlap of the funding series and the archive; prices read before)

studies.pass_rule: Sharpe ≥ 0.5 AND funding paid ≤ 40% of gross profit AND max drawdown ≤ half of BTC buy-and-hold's, net of costs and real funding.
studies.verdict: passes on the pre-registered window (Sharpe 0.88, funding 14.5% of gross profit as read and 18.9% with the gaps filled, drawdown 12.0% against BTC's 76.7%); on the stricter 2021-06 → 2026-06 window the same runs read 0.54 and 0.49. The finding: funding on the coin-days the sleeve held averaged 0.0589%/day against 0.0263%/day over all coin-days, a ratio of 2.24, above 1.5 on every coin — 15–20%/yr of long notional against the 11%/yr the fixed assumption charged. The prediction that real funding would land below the assumption was wrong in direction.
studies.limits: Binance's funding, not Bitget's (CoinAPI's Bitget futures history starts 2023-06); spot prices with a perp's funding and without the perp's basis gain, the conservative reading; 24% of held coin-days had no funding sample (charged nothing, counted; the gaps-filled run is the bound the other way); the window's prices were read before.
